title: Bóna's maximal-avoidance conjecture for Hertzsprung patterns
source: Anders Claesson, “From Hertzsprung's problem to pattern-rewriting systems”, arXiv:2012.15309 (2021). (https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.15309)

lanes.final_paper_check: final-paper-check-349250-355132-opus-20261118-r1/CHECK-349250.md (Claude Opus 5.5, PASS WITH EDITORIAL EDITS; revised paper used)

significance.root_decision: For all k and n and every pattern tau in S_k, the number of permutations of [n] with no Hertzsprung occurrence of tau (consecutive positions, values order-isomorphic with a single shift) is at most the number with no Hertzsprung occurrence of the identity pattern of length k; the inequality is strict when k < n and tau is neither the identity nor its reverse. This is the maximal-avoidance conjecture of Bona as stated in Claesson Conjecture 3.13, including the self-overlapping patterns that the earlier argument did not cover. The proof compares first and second moments of occurrence counts.
significance.caveat: The 2008 Discrete Mathematics version of Bona's paper is unread (paywalled). One phrase about work associated with Claesson Conjecture 3.14 carries no citation.
